items.name: Nvidia Flora
items.summary: Nvidia's GEAR lab open-sourced Flora, a trio of models that turn raw robot and human manipulation video into training labels — segmenting actions, captioning them, and scoring outcomes. Nvidia says the suite already labels 200,000 hours of video a day for its GR00T humanoid models at a claimed 125x lower cost than GPT-6 Astra.

items.name: AWS Infinity
items.summary: AWS and UC Berkeley released Infinity, an open-source agent runtime under Apache 2.0 that suspends agents during tool calls instead of holding a process open. The design lets huge numbers of mostly-idle agents share little memory — AWS claims 75,000 concurrent agents fit in 8 GB — and run on serverless platforms even when a tool call takes days.

items.name: Hugging Face Carbon-X
items.summary: Hugging Face released Carbon-X, an open 14.8-billion-parameter model that reads raw DNA sequences inside a chat message and answers in English — predicting mutation effects, classifying sequences, and explaining its reasoning. Released under Apache 2.0, it runs locally on a single 80 GB GPU, so labs can keep sensitive genomic data off cloud APIs.

items.name: Anthropic Claude Duet
items.summary: Anthropic launched Claude Duet, a proactive AI agent built on Claude Opus 5.5 that monitors connected apps, sends a morning brief, and works tasks in the cloud while the user is away. Now in a waitlisted research preview for US Pro and Max subscribers, it requires approval before sensitive actions like payments or deletions.

items.name: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017
items.summary: DeepSeek shipped V4.1-Flash-1017, a new checkpoint of its low-cost long-context model with MIT-licensed open weights and improved scores across every official benchmark, including 77.0 on DeepSWE v1.1. The release also opens DeepSeek's Search and Fetch APIs to all developers at $0.75 per 1,000 calls.
